steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Place drained green beans in a 9x13-inch baking pan.
Arrange bacon in a single layer on a microwave-safe plate. Cook in the microwave until slightly cooked, about 2 minutes. Lay bacon over green beans.
Mix together brown sugar, melted butter, soy sauce, and garlic powder in a small bowl. Pour over green beans and bacon.
Bake, uncovered, in the preheated oven for 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Arkansas Green Beans
raw_recipe.description: These brown sugar green beans are made with canned green beans and bacon cooked in garlic butter and sweet soy sauce for an irresistible side dish.
raw_recipe.name: Arkansas Green Beans

review.reviewBody: oh my!, these are really, really good. I used fresh green beans and fresh garlic. I cut the sugar in half and it was fine(always find recipes to be to sweet). I will be making these again and they will show up on the holiday table. Caught my son dipping bread in the sauce. Thanks for sharing. YUM, YUM!!

Oh. My. God. So I have to be honest. I picked this recipe over the various others because of the fact that you bake it. This is much easier when making a large Christmas dinner. I was VERY worried how it would taste, the brown sugar part was making everyone make faces. So I took the suggestion of others and halved the brown sugar. As I was worried about the sauce permeating through all the beans, I also added 50% more sauce. Turns out this second part was not needed, but taking the brown sugar down by half was. IT WAS PERFECT. Everyone LOVED it. The only other changes I made was that I did cut the bacon into smaller pieces before microwaving, but I still layed it on top, and used enough to cover the beans. I also used frozen beans, and 4 bags worked well. We will definitely be using this recipe again!
Excellent! I used fresh green beans and halved the brown sugar. (If using fresh green beans, cover the dish when baking to allow the beans to steam.) A keeper!

really good! I halved the recipe for 3 people, 5 servings. I cooked the bacon about 1/2 way in a pan, then cut into smaller pieces, added to 2 cans of green beans into a 8x8 baking dish, then tossed to coat with the sauce. I tasted a bean 1/2 way thru cooking and added more soy sauce to make it less sweet. My boyfriend really liked, and ate the extras :)

This is one of the best green bean recipes I have ever tasted. I cook for a homeless shelter once a month and I made these beans to go with their meal and everyone loved them. I also have made them for a church potluck and there wasn't a single bean left. The only thing I do differently with the recipe is that I completely cook the bacon ahead of time, crumble it and add it to the green beans before I pour the butter mixture over them. This recipe is definitely a keeper!
Yum! I will definitely use this recipe again. I used fresh green beans, about 1.5 lbs i think and cut the other ingredients in half. I wish i made more. It was very good.

Delicious as written but three notes: 1. Definitely 1/2 the brown sugar unless you like candied green beans 2. Fry & crumble the bacon before adding (or use real bacon bits), otherwise the bacon stays limp 3. Frozen green beans will work instead of canned

These were fantastic. Sweet, smoky, with that umami from the soy sauce. Maybe a tad bit too sweet, so I'd cut back on the sugar a tiny bit. I think next time instead of using whole strips of bacon on top, I'll chop it up as it was difficult to serve with the whole strip, even though it looked fancy. I took a pair of kitchen shears and cut through it in several places so I could dish this up properly. The flavor was really good, and I cut this half for 4 servings. I just used a 28 oz. can of green beans because it's what I had on hand and I wasn't going to run out to the store because I was half a can short. I made it work and it was great. I'd make this again. It was easy and most of all, it was different from our usual. ***I made this again for a potluck meal and used a full third cup of dark brown sugar plus just over half of the second third cup, cut the bacon into pieces after partially cooking it in the microwave, and cut back on the soy by 1 T as the soy flavor was pretty forward the first time. This was perfect!!! Not too sweet, no noticable soy flavor, and easy to serve with the bacon in smaller pieces. I might have added a few twists of black pepper, but that's it. These might be my new favorite green beans. This was disappearing off the table faster than the green bean casseroles.

I made this with only 3 cans and it still had enough for me, my husband, and 2 of my kids to have seconds, plus leftovers. I cut the sugar down to only 1/4 cup and it was still a bit too sweet for us so will do a little less next time. Cut the soy sauce down to 3 1/2 tsp and garlic to 1 tsp since we used less beans than it called for. Used 6 slices of bacon but cooked on the stove until crispy, crumbled them, and mixed them in with the beans instead of on top. And I mixed the sauce in with the beans as well. Except for it being a bit sweeter than I like, it came out really good and everyone went for seconds. Will make again.

7.14.20 ...I went with these amounts: 1½# fresh green beans, 2 slices bacon, 1/3c brown sugar, ¼c melted butter, 1T soy sauce, ½t granulated garlic. After removing the bacon, I halfcooked the beans in some of the bacon fat; added the remaining ingredients & continued to saute. 'Returned the bacon to the pan near the end. E, 23, had TWO servings! :O Next time, 2T butter, 2T brown sugar. He also had two servings of this ... https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/21342/calico-squash-casserole/ ... I realize my review is more of my recipe than submitter's, but there isn't a place for notes anywhere else. :o

Not really sure how to rate this since I didn't actually try it myself. The only thing I did different to the recipe was to use 100oz. of green beans instead of 75oz. Took it to a church potluck. My mom said that there was too much green beans to get the full effect of the flavor. She also said it was too sweet. I will have to make it again soon using the right amount of green beans for just my family and see what they think of it. Next time I will probably cut up the bacon and mix it throughout instead of just laying it on top in whole slices, and lessen the brown sugar by a little bit. This was definitely very easy to make and I'm sure it will be a yummy dish once I use all the right proportions.
My daughter and I have been making them for afew years and they are the best Can also be cooked in crock pot. We also marinate them before cooking.
My family likes green beans now.

I am not a green bean person but these are Absolutely delicious!! Just the right amount of sweet and savory to do the trick. I will have this one on the back of the cubbard door fory grandkids to enjoy!! Thank you for changing my mind about green beans!

I had decided to make these when I realized I did not have bacon. But I had bacon grease. So I added 2 tbs of the bacon grease to the sugar mixture. They were delicious. Next time I will make sure I have bacon. Thanks for the recipe.

I did half the brown sugar and the garlic powder. I cut the bacon in bite sized pieces and cooked in a skillet before putting on top of the beans. The bacon was nice and crispy that way. I made this for a family that always had the traditional green beans with crsipy onions on top so I was nervous mine might not go over. BUT, it was a hit and they want it again next year!!
Everyone loves it. I pre-fry the bacon, chop it up into bits and add along with bacon grease to the top of the green beans.
I used frozen green beans so had to add a little liquid (chicken broth). It was definitely sweet so would cut down on sugar next time. I added a little pepper as well.
